Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I've attached a short evidence packet and a failover sequence diagram. Priyom (solutions/infra) is on cc and will add technical detail where needed. Grace (CS) will run the tabletop once we lock a date.

Summary answers (short):
- RTO/RPO: For our Redwood Hosted API we publish operational commitments: typical cross-az failover RTO under 90s, RPO = 0 for user data persisted to our durable store (client tokens/embeddings) and best-effort for in-flight token cache. Cross-region failovers are targeted RTO under 10 minutes in a full-region outage; RPO depends on replication window (default 30s for event streams, configurable down to 5s with dedicated pipelines).
- Failover sequencing: automatic routing and fallback for stateless requests; stateful sessions use a staged failover: 1) traffic re-routing, 2) KV prefix rehydration, 3) session continuity reconciliation. Human approval only required for failback or when data-migration operations exceed threshold (we flag and notify).
- KV/session state: KV cache not journaled across all model types; we persist checkpointed session state to durable storage at configurable intervals. See attached runbook excerpt for rehydration steps.
- Long running sessions: streaming sessions may see a short reconnection window; our SDKs support reconnect/resume semantics. For sessions longer than 10 minutes with consistent token ordering we recommend a sticky routing policy or dedicated capacity to avoid cross-instance replays.

Attachments included: AbbeyLane-RTO-RPO-Statement.pdf, failover-sequence-2028-03.svg

We can provide the tabletop exercise plan and proposed dates; sending a short proposal in a follow-up.

Maya, Connor — quick technical clarifications and additional detail to supplement Connor's note. I'm including the failover SVG as an attachment and a small table of deterministic behavior by failure class below.

Failure class mapping (excerpt):
- Single-instance GPU crash (within AZ): automatic restart on same pool; session cache best-effort rehydrate; expected < 90s impact.
- AZ-level loss: autoscaler spins up pre-warmed instances in same region, router moves traffic; RTO < 90s for stateless. For stateful: prefix rehydration + reconcile window of up to 3 minutes depending on prefix size.
- Region-level outage: traffic is re-routed to a paired region; replication lag defines RPO (default 30s). We keep a prioritized queue for KV rehydration to reduce critical session impact. Target full availability in target region < 10 mins for our multi-region customers using cross-region replication.

Notes on rehydration: we persist checkpoints to a write-ahead store. During failover we apply prefix-based fetch ordering (hot prefixes first). If you need guaranteed zero-loss for in-flight tokens we recommend configuring a replication factor and sync window (we can propose concrete numbers against your workload).

I'll attach a short runbook excerpt (in the shared Drive link) and can provide raw logs from an internal rehearsal under NDA if needed.

Attachments: failover-sequence-2028-03.svg
